discussion_comments.comment_body:
[P2] Preserve an explicit Azure environment token budget

The `assumeModernModel` branch discards an explicitly supplied `OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS` along with the built-in default. With `OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS=73`, no `OPENAI_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS`, and `new AzureChatCompletionProvider('internal-deployment', ...)`, the old request has `max_tokens: 73`; the new request has neither token-limit field. A recognizable `o3` deployment still sends `max_completion_tokens: 73`.

This loses a user-specified budget merely because the deployment is named opaquely, despite the stated preservation of Azure fallback behavior. Please distinguish the injected 1,024 default from an explicitly set Azure environment limit: omit the former for unknown aliases while retaining the latter under the selected token field. Add an opaque-deployment test with only `OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS` set.

If dropping this setting on Azure is intentional, please describe it as a compatibility change rather than claiming Azure fallback preservation.

[P2] Preserve provider-layer precedence through loadApiProvider

Could we preserve the distinction between suite env and explicit provider env here, and cover the normal loader in the regression? `createApiProvider` merges suite `context.env` into `providerOptions.env`, which reaches this resolver as the first `env` layer. With a registered provider-layer `OPENAI_API_KEY=provider-key`, calling `loadApiProvider` with suite `env: { OPENAI_API_KEY: 'suite-key' }` therefore still selects `suite-key` before reaching the new provider layer. The direct-constructor test bypasses that merge, so it does not verify the provider-over-suite precedence promised for ordinary loaded providers. Explicit provider overrides should keep their existing priority.

Clarified the scope in 2e6b430cb2. The convenience numberOfResults setting overrides the count in the top-level retrievalConfiguration. A complete retrieveAndGenerateConfiguration retains precedence over generated convenience settings; its count belongs inside knowledgeBaseConfiguration.retrievalConfiguration.vectorSearchConfiguration. SDK wire controls confirm that precedence, so this correction changes documentation only.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in 77c0d51fd6: the flag is applied after `extra_args`, so a caller's value cannot replace it. The options test covers an `extra_args` that sets it.

Clarified the units and precedence in d4a3deb12a: native config.maxRetries counts additional retries, whereas the existing AWS_BEDROCK_MAX_RETRIES environment variable is passed through as total SDK attempts, including the initial request. The environment behavior predates this PR, so I preserved it. A 24-case SDK wire matrix confirms env values 0/1 make one request, env 2 permits a retry, explicit config wins, and stateful operations always use one attempt. The change is documentation-only; runtime code and tests are unchanged.

The endpoint follows explicit config, provider AWS_REGION, then the documented us-east-1 default. Four public-provider controls verify those choices while preserving the model ARN. A pinned-main Converse control sends the same west-region ARN to the east default as well. AWS defines the source Region by the endpoint; it does not require clients to infer that endpoint from the ARN. Callers can explicitly select the intended region. Automatic ARN-based endpoint selection would be a new default policy rather than a fix to the advertised ARN preservation behavior.

discussion_comments.comment_body: The [AWS Opus 5.5 card](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-anthropic-claude-opus-5-5.html) does limit current Mantle availability to the listed regions. The provider defaults to supported `us-east-1`, and the documentation directs users to that availability table. Selecting `eu-west-1` is an unsupported model/region combination, not a supported route broken by this change. I am leaving AWS authoritative for region availability instead of adding another exhaustive local allowlist that can become stale or reject custom endpoints. Better fail-fast messaging for unsupported regions can be considered separately.
